blockers.detail: Per-repo Oracle engineering was attempted twice and both public-surface designs are provably impossible on this task. (1) The accepted change deletes internal/app/handlers/handlers.go and adds controller.go/get.go/middleware.go/post.go; including that deletion in the source-only golden fixes the duplicate-declaration compile error, but the exported handler constructor then diverges: start has NewController(config.Config, *database.DataBase) while golden has NewController(config.Config, *database.DataBase, chan worker.OrderStr) and the worker package does not exist at the start revision, so no single handler-level test compiles on both revisions (golden compile error: 'not enough arguments in call to handlers.NewController'). (2) At the database level the accepted change replaces the DataBase.Err struct of error values with package-level sentinels: at start, an externally constructed DataBase has a zero Err, so a Luhn-invalid order returns HTTP 202 and nil error, while at golden it returns ErrBadOrderNumber - the observable behaviour itself differs, and reaching the start behaviour requires the removed unexported type errs. The only cross-revision test the earlier attempt found called the unexported checkOrderNumber directly, which is forbidden private-helper binding and would fail a correct refactor.
blockers.resolution: would require a solution-coupled or private-binding Oracle, or accepting an Oracle whose expected behaviour differs between the start and golden revisions; both are excluded by the hard-Oracle standard

blockers.detail: An Ember/QUnit Oracle was engineered and is behaviourally strict: it renders the reviewed job-status panel in real headless Chromium and asserts the observable DOM for the three deployment cases, passing 3/3 on the exact start revision and 3/3 on the source-only golden, fully offline, with Node 16.20.0 pinned by the official SHASUMS256.txt and a --frozen-lockfile node_modules tree packaged as caches/node_modules.tar.gz. blockers.detail: An Oracle for this task is engineered and behaviourally strict: it executes the project's own sbt build offline against a pinned, fully hashed ivy/coursier closure and passes 3/3 on the exact start revision and 3/3 on the golden, with a nonempty named PASS_TO_PASS set. It is nevertheless non-scoring because changed-old production line coverage cannot be measured during the validation run: the pinned JaCoCo 0.8.12 agent attaches to the sbt JVM (-J-javaagent) and does produce an exec plus an XML report over 1,469 analysed classes, but the reviewed production source reports zero covered lines (the classes the report analyses are not the class identities the tests actually executed), and the alternative injection path `set every Test/javaOptions += -javaagent:...` fails the scala-js build outright. The historical JaCoCo measurement is retained as informational evidence only and, per the hard-Oracle standard, cannot satisfy the coverage requirement.
blockers.resolution: attach JaCoCo so the executed class identities match the analysed class files (e.g. a build-level coverage plugin pinned for this revision), then re-run validate-oracle; the recipe is retained verbatim and needs no other change
